ocr_text: <ocr>SELECTION OF PACKAGE FOR CAMEL FILTER It was unanimously agreed in a meeting of Messrs. W. S. Smith, W. A. Sugg, C. H. Judge, Howard Gray, R. A. Rechholtz, R. M. Odear, and R. A. Blevins that the brown package presents the best oppor- tunity in which to market CAMEL Filter. The brown package was selected over the foil package for the following reasons: 1. Based on shipments, CAMEL Filter's share of market was higher in markets having the brown package than markets having the foil package in the North, in the South, and combined (Table I). 2. Based on Inventory Service data, CAMEL Filter's share of market R was higher in markets having the brown package than markets having the foil package in the North, in the South, and combined ; (Table I). ' 3. CAMEL Filter contributed more additional business to the combined sales of CAMEL, CAMEL Filter, and WINSTON in the brown markets than in the foil markets (Table II). 4. The brown package gained more business from competitive brands than the foil based on both Inventory Service and shipment data (Table III). 5. The brown had more appeal to men than the foil which we consider to be an advantage to the brown (Table IV). The foil package had a more feminine appeal than the brown which we consider to be a negative for the foil. It follows that the brown package would have greater appeal to average-to-heavy smokers, and the foil package to light smokers. 6. The brown package was more strongly projected as a rich tobacco tasting cigarette than the foil (Table IV). The foil package was projected as being a mild cigarette. 7. while an image study suggested that the foil package would have greater appeal to young smokers, when offered packages of CAMEL Filter and asked to choose among them, smokers aged 21 to 24 selected the brown about the same as the foil package. Smokers 25 and over significantly preferred the brown to the.foil package (Table V). 8.
